correctness.rationale: Factor X^n−1 into distinct integral cyclotomic factors Phi_d of degree φ(d). Degree completeness is exactly the subset-sum fullness of the coin multiset {φ(d):d|n}. An odd φ-practical n must be divisible by 3 to obtain degree 2 and by 5 to obtain degree 4; write n=3^a5^bq^c. The largest coin φ(n)=8(q−1)T, with T=3^{a−1}5^{b−1}q^{c−1}, and the sum of the other coins n−φ(n) implies (q−16)T≤1; hence q in {7,11,13,17}, with q=17 forcing T=1 and n=255. For q≤13, the base 15q interval is complete, and exact two-prime cofactor max-gap identities Δ(3^a5^b)=3^{a−1}5^{b−1}, Δ(3^aq^c)=(q−4)3^{a−1}q^{c−1}, Δ(5^bq^c)=(3q−8)5^{b−1}q^{c−1} give sufficient overlap for adding arbitrary further powers of any of three primes. The proof uses a precise subset-sum union gap lemma and induction on exponents, not exhaustive finite exponent testing. Independent exact bitsets checked 64 representative q,exponent cases and 96 two-prime gap formulas; all matched.

evidence: Thompson (2011), Lemma 4.1: when p∤M and M is φ-practical, adjoining p or p^k is governed by p≤M+2 or p≤M+1; Corollary 4.2 characterizes squarefree φ-practical numbers.
Pomerance–Thompson–Weingartner (2016) cite the same extension conditions, but stress there is no universal simple prime-growth criterion for all φ-practical integers.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General prime-adjoining results imply some q-side sufficiency cases but not classification of all positive exponents a,b,c with repeated factors 3,5. The necessary largest-coin obstruction and exact two-prime gap induction supply a nontrivial complete characterization.

evidence: Thompson’s Lemma 4.1 immediately handles new-prime powers q^c once 15 is φ-practical; its squarefree results cover 15q when q≤17.
However increasing exponents of already-present 3,5 under fixed q is not covered by the cited p∤M lemma; the proof calculates and controls cofactor gaps for all exponents.

evidence: Thompson 2011 §1 defines φ-practical as X^n−1 having a factor of each degree 0..n, equivalent to completeness of subset sums of φ(d), d|n.
The conclusion is specifically for ω(n)=3 and odd n, not generic practical integers, weakly φ-practical integers, or 2-dense integers.

originality.rationale: Thompson (2011) defined and studied φ-practical numbers, the squarefree criterion and Lemma 4.1 for adjoining a new prime (including prime powers); Pomerance–Thompson–Weingartner (2016) refined general asymptotics and primer-extension rules. Those are decisive precedents for the definition and some sufficiency directions, e.g. 15q and powers of a newly added q. Neither materially inspected full source states the exact odd support size-three classification with the {7,11,13} infinite exponent families and solitary 255, nor an all-three-exponents cofactor-gap proof. General prime-extension rules do not literally give arbitrary exponents of 3 and 5 when those primes already divide the number. A stronger known support theorem or table remains a residual risk; the novelty assertion is only the sharp bounded-support classification.
residual_risks: The general φ-practical literature may contain an equivalent classification for bounded support not indexed by the phrase three prime factors.
The prior new-prime extension lemma covers parts of the claimed sufficiency, so only the remaining exponent-uniform sharp support theorem should be represented as new.

value.rationale: Prime-factor support is the natural finite-complexity parameter in φ-practical-number theory, where no simple universal Stewart-like classification exists. The complete three-distinct-prime classification determines an infinite set of integer families and a sharp isolated exception, with an exact gap mechanism that distinguishes prime-power extensions. It is a motivated natural cutoff, not an arbitrary small-integer check.

limitations: Only odd n with exactly three distinct prime divisors; even n, two-prime support and larger support are outside the theorem.
The exact bitset tests cover bounded exponents and primes; the universal classification uses analytic gap induction.
